Ratings collapse a large scenario ladder to one word. The DSA write-up also needs the **paths**: PV of debt-to-GDP, PV of debt-to-revenue, debt service-to-revenue, debt service-to-GDP, and the Figure 1 / Figure 2 series that plot baseline, historical average, MX shock, and threshold.

Those functions return a `Series` (a labeled tensor). `as_records` turns the tensor into a list of dictionaries that pandas or polars can ingest.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import Model, api, as_records

case = Model.from_defaults()
```

## Public-debt stress ladder

`compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp` is the Chart Data block that starts at row 239: one path per scenario, years 2024–2044.

```{python}
pv_gdp = case.chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp
list(pv_gdp.domain.axes[0].keys)
```

```{python}
{
    "2024": pv_gdp.sel(SCENARIO="Baseline", TIME_PERIOD=2024),
    "2034": pv_gdp.sel(SCENARIO="Baseline", TIME_PERIOD=2034),
}
```

On the shipped snapshot, public PV of debt-to-GDP starts near 67 percent of GDP and declines to about 45 percent by 2034 under the baseline.

`as_records` uses the function’s published key (`SCENARIO`, `TIME_PERIOD`) and names the measure `OBS_VALUE`:

```{python}
records = as_records(
    api.compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp,
    pv_gdp,
)
ladder = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)
wide = (
    ladder.loc[ladder["TIME_PERIOD"].between(2024, 2029)]
    .pivot(index="TIME_PERIOD", columns="SCENARIO", values="OBS_VALUE")
    .loc[:, ["Baseline", "B1. Real GDP growth", "B2. Primary balance", "B3. Exports"]]
)
wide
```

The same pattern applies to the other three public-debt blocks:

| Metric | Function |
| --- | --- |
| PV of debt-to-GDP | `compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp` |
| PV of debt-to-revenue | `compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_revenue_ratio_pv_debt_to_revenue` |
| Debt service-to-revenue | `compute_chart_output_chart_data_debt_service_to_revenue_ratio_debt_service_to_revenue` |
| Debt service-to-GDP | `compute_chart_output_chart_data_debt_service_to_gdp_ratio_debt_service_gdp_ratio` |

Each is keyed by the standard scenario ladder: Baseline, A1 historical, B1–B6, C1–C4, and the A2 customized title.

## Figure 1 / Figure 2 series

The stress-chart functions use a shorter scenario list — the rows the workbook actually plots. `compute_chart_output_pv_debt_gdp_ratio` is the external PV of debt-to-GDP chart: baseline, historical, MX shock, one-year MX, and the threshold.

```{python}
figure = case.chart_output_pv_debt_gdp_ratio
list(figure.domain.axes[0].keys)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "External PV of PPG debt to GDP — baseline, most-extreme shock, and threshold (template snapshot)."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of external PV of debt-to-GDP for 2024–2044 under the baseline, the MX shock, and the LIC-DSF threshold."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

years = list(figure.domain.axes[1].keys)
series = {
    "Baseline": [figure.sel(SCENARIO="Baseline", TIME_PERIOD=year) for year in years],
    "MX shock": [
        figure.sel(SCENARIO="MX shock Standard&Tailored", TIME_PERIOD=year)
        for year in years
    ],
    "Threshold": [figure.sel(SCENARIO="Threshold", TIME_PERIOD=year) for year in years],
}

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for label, values in series.items():
    ax.plot(years, values, label=label)
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("PV of debt to GDP")
ax.legend()
ax.set_title("External DSA — PV of debt to GDP")
fig
```

The public-debt analogue is `compute_chart_output_pv_debt_to_gdp`. Companion figure helpers cover PV of debt-to-exports, debt service-to-exports, and debt service-to-revenue (`compute_chart_output_pv_debt_to_exports`, `compute_chart_output_debt_service_to_exports`, `compute_chart_output_debt_service_to_revenue`).

## Customized A2 as its own series

When you only need the customized-enter path, use the dedicated A2 function. It is keyed by `TIME_PERIOD` alone:

```{python}
a2 = case.chart_pv_debt_gdp_ratio_custom_alternative_scenario
pd.DataFrame(
    as_records(api.compute_chart_pv_debt_gdp_ratio_custom_alternative_scenario, a2)
).head()
```

On the snapshot the A2 path matches the baseline until you fill `customized_public_delta` — see [Stress tests and what-ifs](stress-tests-and-what-ifs.qmd).

## Realism tools and the probability approach

Chart Data is not the only published surface. Realism 1–4 and the Probability approach sheets supply the series behind Output 4 and Output 6. They use the same `from_defaults` / `Model` pattern.

The three-year fiscal-adjustment placement on Realism 4 is a scalar:

```{python}
{
    "label": case.realism4_projected_3yr_adjustment_label,
    "adjustment": case.realism4_projected_3yr_adjustment,
}
```

Probability-approach PV of debt-to-GDP is a `SCENARIO` × `TIME_PERIOD` series over the same 2024–2044 grid as Chart Data:

```{python}
prob = case.probability_pv_debt_to_gdp
{
    "baseline_2024": prob.sel(SCENARIO="Baseline", TIME_PERIOD=2024),
    "threshold_2024": prob.sel(SCENARIO="Threshold", TIME_PERIOD=2024),
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
`as_records(compute, result)` needs the **function**, not only the result. The function carries `__key__` and `__domain__`; the tensor carries the values. Passing the wrong function raises a domain mismatch.
:::
